coaching.headline: They won most of the fights. We took their base without losing an inhibitor. A proper fucking comeback.
coaching.team: Down four towers before we had taken one of theirs, with two Fangtooths and a Genesis Core gone the same way, the map was theirs. Then the big prizes went the other way: both Primal Fangtooths, Orb Prime, three inhibitors and the Core. Three of our four won fights became an objective or structure; they converted half of their ten. We also took a tower and the first Primal Fangtooth in the same windows as fights we lost. Taking the map, more than winning fights, is how this flipped.

focus.title: One down, don't force it
focus.evidence: Twice one of us died outside any fight shortly before a fight we then lost, and both times their Fangtooth or a tower followed.
focus.action: When one of us dies before a Fangtooth or tower comes up, the other four fall back to the next tower instead of fighting a body down. Next game, count their takes right after one of our deaths outside a fight.

perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Goldilocks324 ran the most complete game on our side, and it was not fucking close. Gideon beat his own usual farm and damage on the hero, finished richest in the lobby, and took kills off four different enemies, Legion three times. That is the standard. Argus and Khaimera split his four deaths, and both Argus kills came outside any recorded fight. When Argus has not shown and Gideon has to cross the map, keep the portal for the exit.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs took Khaimera down four times, more than anyone else on our side, and led our objective damage by a distance. That is jungle pressure with actual teeth. Ten deaths is a hell of a bill, though, and two of them came outside any recorded fight shortly before each of their Fangtooths. Next game, when Fangtooth is about a minute out, Feng Mao paths toward the pit and waits for the team's call before taking any new trade.
perPlayer.08bea990-2b35-47e0-85a5-93f4545532c2: A rough night for MarKnoop, and it does not need dressing up. Sparrow gave up first blood to Legion, died more than twice the usual count on less than the usual damage, and Khaimera had Sparrow on speed dial for four of the seven. The Khaimera kill in the second Primal Fangtooth fight is the one to build on. When Khaimera is unseen, Sparrow plays behind Maco, the front-line build, and holds Heightened Senses as the answer to the leap.
perPlayer.b5210bcc-5219-4b31-b552-f4943b07e036: Maco did the support job that shows up on paper: the most healing in the lobby, our highest mitigation, more wards than Argus and a hand in over half our kills. The bodies were the cost. Khaimera killed him four times, and one death outside any fight came just before our first tower and their first Fangtooth fell. When Khaimera leaps onto Sparrow or Maco, Maco fires Phantom Rush for speed and slow immunity on the way out.
perPlayer.f3790729-823f-4410-98f5-287108c302b0: Iggy & Scorch owned our most lopsided win: Argus, Terra and Khaimera in one exchange, then two of their inner towers and an inhibitor fell. Damage ran about a third above his usual on the hero, and he took the last kill before the Core. Terra was the recurring problem, credited with three of his five deaths. Terra's ultimate cleanses debuffs and adds both armors for several seconds, so Iggy & Scorch holds Inferno until that buff ends.

19.4.call: Khaimera killed Maco and Terra killed Iggy & Scorch, lost 0-2, and their second Fangtooth followed. Feng Mao had died just before, outside the cluster. The timing does not show where anyone stood or whether the pit was contestable.

31.7.call: Won 4-1: Iggy & Scorch took Argus, Terra and Khaimera, Gideon took Legion, and Khaimera got Gideon. Two inner towers and an inhibitor of theirs fell shortly after. Kill credits do not show who hit those structures.

36.5.call: Won 3-2 as we took the second Primal Fangtooth; Feng Mao and Iggy & Scorch died in it. An inhibitor, Orb Prime and the Core followed. The timing does not show who was at the pit or who finished the Core.

matchup: Gadget roots with Security Gate and added Spellbreaker's spell shield.
Argus was credited with two of Gideon's four deaths, and Khaimera's leap threatens a caster whose only escape is the portal.
build: Azure Core, Combustion and Wraith Leggings is the common winning mid core, and he had all three.
Tainted Scepter has real targets in Khaimera's lifesteal and Legion's Nightfall.
Spellbreaker blocks one ability, such as Gadget's root or Argus's stun.
eternal: Vesh suits a long game, Tithe of Death pays on takedowns, and Phylactery shields after Black Hole.
Mind Rot is the slot-two alternative when raw damage matters more than the shield; nothing shows the shield was wasted.
augment: Infinite Impact turns the comet into long-range poke and a slow that can reach a fleeing target.
Event Horizon is the alternative into a health-stacking front like Terra; this game does not prove either better.
crest: Epoch's stasis answers Khaimera's leap or Argus's burst when the portal is spent, at the cost of standing still.
The deaths cannot be tied to whether it was available.
improvement: Keep it: the winning core plus two situational items with clear targets in this draft.
If Khaimera becomes the main threat, compare a physical-armor item over Spellbreaker, which does nothing against basic attacks.
This win does not prove the swap.

matchup: Khaimera healed off his damage, built Terminus and Mutilator, and had the most kills in the match.
Gank targets carried answers: Legion's Mesmer and Nightfall, Terra's Stonewall and Vainglory armor.
build: Manta Scythe, Omen and The Perforator is the standard winning core for jungle Feng Mao.
The Perforator matters into Terra's armor; Tainted Trident directly answers Khaimera's lifesteal and Legion's Nightfall.
eternal: Demiurge and Tri-Core suit an item-driven bruiser.
Cursed Corrupted had little or nothing to convert, since none of the five finished items carries critical chance.
Bloatware is the slot-two option that pays without crit.
augment: Ichorous Glaive heals on unit kills and Earth Shatter executions, paying on clears, not during the trade.
Imperial Duelist is the alternative when extended duels with Khaimera are the problem.
crest: Ortus rewards entering a fight about to produce kills, like the Khaimera takedowns.
As an escape it only offers speed.
improvement: Keep Manta Scythe, Omen, The Perforator and Tainted Trident while Khaimera is the jungle opponent.
Free loadout fix: swap Cursed Corrupted for Bloatware, since the build gave crit conversion nothing to use.
It is not a claim that any particular death would have been prevented.

matchup: Legion took first blood on Sparrow and built Mesmer, Nightfall and Tainted Trident.
Khaimera, with four of Sparrow's seven deaths, was the bigger threat to a carry whose only escape is a short stealth.
Terra's Stonewall and Vainglory stacked armor in front.
build: Storm Breaker and Sky Splitter are two-thirds of the winning core; Spectra is the missing piece.
Sky Splitter still chews through a tanky front like Terra, and Vanquisher executes very low-health heroes.
eternal: Weald rewards finishing, Forage adds farm income, and Wind-Rider fits the kit via Heightened Senses stealth.
Natural Resistance is the slot-one alternative when Khaimera's stun ends fights, at the cost of Forage's farm.
augment: Sun Shards stacks with Storm Breaker and Onixian Quiver in grouped fights, but adds little when Sparrow is dived.
There is no basis to call Inner Fury or Endless Hunt a proven upgrade.
crest: Eviscerator is an all-in damage window, not an escape.
Against Khaimera's dives it only helps if Sparrow can keep shooting through them.
improvement: Spectra is the comparison for the Dust Devil slot, trading attack and movement speed against Khaimera for a missing-health burst.
If Khaimera keeps reaching Sparrow, compare Natural Resistance over Forage, a low-health cleanse for farm income.
The deaths alone do not prove which change would have helped more.

matchup: Argus pokes from range with a stun; Legion took first blood.
Khaimera, credited with four of Maco's deaths, was the real pressure on the duo.
Gadget's Tesla Dome adds a heavy slow to any grouped fight.
build: Maco skipped the common support core for a front-line kit; Tainted Guard cuts Khaimera's healing when he attacks.
It fits our highest mitigation, but does not prove the build won or lost any fight.
eternal: Knell pays when Maco is in the fight hitting heroes; Patina is a between-fights cushion.
Resonant Repair fits Khaimera's stun and Argus's control.
The field most often runs Exarch; this match cannot say whether it would have done more.
augment: Ferocious Flight pays twice when the slam hits several enemies: more shielding and a faster next leap.
Shatterbloom is the alternative when sustaining a grouped team matters more than surviving the front.
crest: Leafsong's Phantom Rush is a group engage or escape button against Gadget's, Argus's and Khaimera's slows.
The extra ward slot fits Maco out-warding Argus.
improvement: If Khaimera keeps reaching the duo, compare Enra's Blessing over Claw Of Hermes, trading mana-burn damage for a reactive save for Sparrow.
This win does not prove the swap was needed.

matchup: Terra stacked both armors, and Tainted Bastion cuts healing of anyone hitting her with magical damage.
Terra got three of Iggy & Scorch's five deaths and had the highest mitigation in the match.
Khaimera's leap is the other threat to an immobile zone mage.
build: Megacosm's health burn fits Terra, and Magnify shreds the magical armor from Tainted Bastion and Cybernetic Drive.
Vanquisher's physical power, penetration and crit add little to a magical damage dealer.
eternal: Knell is rare here, where Vesh is usual, but shreds both armors on a resist-stacking Terra.
Vesh with Lich trades the shred for burn and lifesteal, which Tainted Bastion would cut on Terra.
augment: Turret Maniac adds a turret at the cost of turret health: more fireballs and more sources of Ignite.
Hold This! is the alternative for a long game; nothing proves it would have done more.
crest: Soulbearer is a window to survive and keep burning against Terra or Khaimera, not an escape.
Its lifesteal is cut whenever he hits Terra while Tainted Bastion is active.
improvement: Vanquisher is the slot to rethink; everything else has a target in this draft.
Entropy, part of the winning core, trades a low-health execute for steady magical damage on every ability hit.
This win does not prove the swap; it shows where the free value sits.

threats: Chain-CC risk (1 hard-CC abilities, ~1.0s of lockdown): Gadget Security Gate (root 1s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Iggy & Scorch Inferno (knockback). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Maco) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

khaimera.loadout: Thraex (Savage Strikes + Ferocity), augment Jungle Invasion, crest Iceskorn Talons
ultPlus: Ashbringer (Chrono Strikes): On Successful Basic Attack: Decrease current Non-Ultimate Cooldowns by 8% On-Hit.• Reduced to 4% against Non-Heroes.• Only triggers once per ability.• Critical Strikes grant 1.5x the cooldown reduction.
lines: Lead story: Damage well above normal. 1,323 hero damage a minute, more than 98% of Khaimera jungle players this patch (28% of the team's). The damage came from Sky Splitter, Imperator, Onixian Quiver.
Cull at rank 3: 60s base, about 48s by the end (20% shorter) from 25 ability haste: Ashbringer 10, Mutilator 15.

Ashbringer (Chrono Strikes): On Successful Basic Attack: Decrease current Non-Ultimate Cooldowns by 8% On-Hit.• Reduced to 4% against Non-Heroes.• Only triggers once per ability.• Critical Strikes grant 1.5x the cooldown reduction.
Their build heals off damage: anti-heal (the Tainted items) cuts it.
Khaimera dealt 52,924 hero damage, 28% of their team's, with +262 physical power from items.
Sky Splitter (item): On Successful Basic Attacks: Deal 5% of Target's Current Health as Damage On-Hit. Reduced to 3.5% for Ranged Heroes. Minimum of 12 Damage.
Imperator (item): Critical Strikes deal 30% more damage.
Onixian Quiver (item): On Ranged Basic Attack: Fire 2 additional projectiles. Each deals 10-35% (increases with Range) () Damage. Can Critically Strike and apply Lifesteal.
Onixian Quiver (item): On Melee Heroes only: Increase your Total Critical Strike Chance by 25%. Gain 1% Damage Mitigation for every 10% Missing Health.
Mutilator (item): On Successsful Basic Attacks: Deal 1% of their Max Health as Damage.

Thraex (Eternal): Mark the last Enemy Hero damaged by your Basic Attack for 3s, increasing your damage against them by 3% (+0.4% per level) and reducing the damage they deal to you by 1.5% (+0.35% per level).

Sustain: 29% lifesteal; 16% omnivamp; Terminus: On Overhealing from Lifesteal: Convert excess Healing into a Shield. Max Shield size: (+100%). The Shield slowly decays 15s after leaving combat.; Savage Strikes: Deal 1.5 (+0.4 per level) Physical Damage On-Hit. Attacking an Enemy Hero increases this by 100% for 3s, stacking up to 3 times. Heal for the damage dealt.; 18,819 healing recorded.
Toughness: +100 health; took 88,736 damage, mitigated 51,659, died 8 times.
Stack (Every basic attack set off): 6 effects on one trigger: Ashbringer, Sky Splitter, Onixian Quiver, Mutilator, Thraex, Savage Strikes.
Stack (Healing off the damage): 6 effects on one trigger: Sky Splitter, Onixian Quiver, Terminus, Mutilator, Iceskorn Talons, Savage Strikes.
Stack (Damage that scales with our health): 2 effects on one trigger: Sky Splitter, Mutilator. The more health a target stacks, the more these deal, so health items on our side fed them.
The Eternal was part of it: Thraex (Savage Strikes + Ferocity) sits on the same triggers as the items (every basic attack set off; healing off the damage), so the same hits paid out twice.

Countered? 3 of the 5 players Khaimera killed built physical armor (Maco, Feng Mao, Iggy & Scorch). Anti-heal on Maco, Iggy & Scorch, Gideon, Feng Mao. Health items on Maco, Iggy & Scorch raised the %-health damage they took. We killed Khaimera 8 times.
Copy it? Thraex (Savage Strikes + Ferocity): 49.5% in 2,930 Khaimera jungle games, below the hero's 51.7%. It wins less than usual elsewhere: it beat us, not the field.

lines: Lead story: Healed through fights. 390 healing a minute, more than 87% of Terra offlane players this patch.
Unstoppable Force at rank 3: 105s base, about 82s by the end (22% shorter) from 28 ability haste: Cybernetic Drive 10, Inquisition 10, Tainted Bastion 8.
Terra dealt 24,511 hero damage, 13% of their team's, with +0 physical power from items.
Cybernetic Drive (item): Against Minions & Small Monsters: Your next Basic Attack On-Hit Executes them. Deals 80 (+5%) Damage to nearby Enemies. Heals you for 30 (+3%).
Inquisition (item): On Ability Cast: Emit a wave of energy. Deals 65 (+1.5%) Damage to Enemies in the area. Damage is increased by 45% against Monsters.
Tainted Bastion (item): On taking Magical Damage: Reduce the Source's Healing by 45% for 3s.
Tainted Bastion (item): Mitigate 3.5% of damage taken. Doubled against Blighted Targets.
Stonewall (item): Mitigate 5 (+5%)% of Physical Damage.
Mending (Eternal minor): After taking Hero damage, restore 3/4/5/6% Missing Health at Levels 1/6/11/16 over 8s.
Iron Resolve (augment): Wild Rush grants 25/27.5/30/32.5/35% Damage Reduction while it is Channeling.

Sustain: 8% heal and shield power; Cybernetic Drive: Against Minions & Small Monsters: Your next Basic Attack On-Hit Executes them. Deals 80 (+5%) Damage to nearby Enemies. Heals you for 30 (+3%).; Tainted Bastion: On taking Magical Damage: Reduce the Source's Healing by 45% for 3s.; Transference: Upon Shields expiring: 50% of its remaining value is restored as Health over 3s. Reduced to 25% for Ally Shields.; 15,609 healing recorded.
Toughness: +1630 health, +163 physical armor, +215 magical armor; took 59,425 damage, mitigated 93,979, died 2 times.
Stack (Healing off the damage): 2 effects on one trigger: Cybernetic Drive, Tainted Bastion.
Countered? 3 of the 3 players Terra killed built physical armor (Iggy & Scorch, Maco, Feng Mao). Anti-heal on Maco, Iggy & Scorch, Gideon, Feng Mao. We killed Terra 2 times.
Copy it? Idrisil: 48.4% in 830 Terra offlane games, level with the hero's 47.8%. A standard setup: what made it work was this game, not a secret build.

sources.note: 2 per takedown, 17 takedowns, capped at 30 from the 15th takedown, around 37 min (estimate)
sources.how: +2 per takedown, up to 30: maxed at takedown 15 (around 37 min)

fedBy: Tainted Scepter (Malice): Once every second: Gain a stack of Malice.• Stacks up to 15 times.• Takedowns grant 15 stacks instantly.• Hitting a Hero with Ability Damage will deal 1.5 (+1%) Damage per stack.
Tithe of Death (minor): Takedowns restore 15% Max Mana and permanently grant 2 Ability Haste, up to 30 Ability Haste.
lines: Lead story: Stayed alive, joined every fight, and each takedown sped up the ultimate. In 61% of the team's kills (more than 88% of Gideon mid players this patch) and died 4 times (fewer than about 66% of them). Tithe of Death turned 17 takedowns into ability haste, so Black Hole came back every ~63s instead of 105s.
Lesson: takedowns were the fuel. Each one Gideon touched shortened Black Hole, so feeding early made it come back faster (about 62.5s late); fight right after Black Hole is spent.
Black Hole at rank 3: 105s base, about 62.5s by the end (40% shorter) from 68 ability haste: Azure Core 10, Tainted Scepter 10, Spellbreaker 10, Epoch 8, Tithe of Death (minor) 30.
Tithe of Death (minor): 2 per takedown, 17 takedowns, capped at 30 from the 15th takedown, around 37 min (estimate).
17 takedowns (7 kills, 10 assists) fed: Tainted Scepter (Malice), Tithe of Death (minor).
Gideon dealt 48,734 hero damage, 31% of their team's, with +555 magical power from items.

Penetration: Wraith Leggings 11, Combustion 9; against Legion (level 18: about 47 magical armor, 27 after penetration; took 15,810 magical damage from heroes, 66% of all hero damage they took) and Argus (level 17: about 47 magical armor, 27 after penetration; took 13,426 magical damage from heroes, 60% of all hero damage they took) that is about 16% and 16% more damage (estimate: percent penetration taken before flat).
Wraith Leggings (item): Against Heroes below 40% Health: Abilities deal 12% bonus Magical Damage.
Combustion (item): On dealing Ability Damage: Deal 50 (+18%) Damage to the Target and nearby Enemies.
Tainted Scepter (item): On Dealing Magical Damage: Reduce the Target's Healing by 45% for 4s.
Tainted Scepter (item): Once every second: Gain a stack of Malice. Stacks up to 15 times. Takedowns grant 15 stacks instantly. Hitting a Hero with Ability Damage will deal 1.5 (+1%) Damage per stack.
Vesh (Eternal): Ability damage dealt to Enemy Heroes deals 7% (+0.4% a minute, about 23% by the end) of that damage as a DoT over 3s.

Sustain: Azure Core: On going below 40% Health: Gain a 100 (+12%) Shield for 5s.; Tainted Scepter: On Dealing Magical Damage: Reduce the Target's Healing by 45% for 4s.; Spellbreaker: Gain a Spell Shield that blocks the next Ability.; 3,285 healing recorded.
Toughness: +200 health, +40 magical armor; took 37,505 damage, mitigated 31,324, died 4 times.
Lesson: Gideon's penetration cut through: Legion took about 16% more magical damage than their armor alone allows (estimate: at level 18 their armor was about 47, about 27 after 20 flat penetration).

Stack (Every ability hit set off): 3 effects on one trigger: Wraith Leggings, Combustion, Vesh. Gideon has 3 damaging abilities (Void Breach, Cosmic Rift, Black Hole hit an area, so one cast sets them off on several heroes), and 68 ability haste brought them back 40% sooner: more casts, more triggers.
Stack (Every takedown fed): 2 effects on one trigger: Tainted Scepter, Tithe of Death. Each kill or assist made the next fight easier.
Stack (Finishing damage on low-health targets): 2 effects on one trigger: Azure Core, Wraith Leggings. Once a fight started going their way, these finished it.
The Eternal was part of it: Vesh (Tithe of Death + Phylactery) sits on the same triggers as the items (every ability hit set off; every takedown fed), so the same hits paid out twice.
Countered? 1 of the 4 players Gideon killed built magical armor (Terra). We killed Gideon 4 times.

Copy it? Vesh (Tithe of Death + Phylactery): 48.7% in 2,298 Gideon midlane games, level with the hero's 48.8%; this 3-item core: 53.6% in 1,250 games, level with the 54.2% of that hero-role's cores. A standard setup: what made it work was this game, not a secret build.

card.lesson: Gideon's takedowns fed Black Hole: every kill or assist made it come back sooner. Deny early takedowns and fight right after Black Hole is used.
